title: Saturating the Bayesian Nagaoka-Hayashi bound within numerical precision for the depolarization SU(2) rotation channel
abstract: The Bayesian Nagaoka--Hayashi (NH) bound is a semidefinite lower bound on the Bayes risk of multiparameter estimation, tighter than the Bayesian symmertic logarithmic derivative (SLD) Cramér--Rao bounds, and whether it can be attained is an open problem. We study the single-shot estimation of a qubit rotation, all three parameters at once, under depolarizing noise and a uniform prior, with $k$ parallel uses of the channel. Rotational covariance reduces the joint optimization of probe, measurement, and estimator, and the NH bound itself, to small semidefinite programs, solvable through $k=4$. At every number of uses and noise strength the optimized strategy reaches the NH bound within the numerical precision of the calculation, numerical evidence that the bound is attained for this channel family, while the SLD bound lies strictly below and is never attained. As the noise grows the optimal probe collapses to the tensored Bell state.
summary: The authors investigate the fundamental limits of estimating multiple parameters characterizing an SU(2) qubit rotation corrupted by noise. They show that the optimized measurement strategy achieves the tight Bayesian Nagaoka-Hayashi bound within numerical precision. This confirms the optimality of the protocol relative to this advanced theoretical limit for the studied channel family.
main_problem: The paper addresses the problem of multiparameter quantum estimation, aiming to find the minimum achievable error (Bayes risk) when estimating several parameters simultaneously using noisy quantum measurements.
main_result: The optimized estimation strategy for a qubit rotation channel under depolarizing noise was shown to attain the Bayesian Nagaoka-Hayashi bound within numerical precision, suggesting this bound is tight for this specific channel family.
method: The problem is formulated as minimizing the weighted Bayesian Mean Square Error (MSE) using Semidefinite Programming (SDP), exploiting rotational symmetry to reduce the complexity of the joint optimization over probe and measurement.
model_or_system: The system models the single-shot estimation of parameters governing an SU(2) qubit rotation channel that is corrupted by depolarizing noise. The analysis considers $k$ parallel uses of this noisy channel.
key_observables: Bayes risk ($ ar{\epsilon}^*$), Bayesian Nagaoka-Hayashi bound ($ ar{\epsilon}_{	ext{NH}}$), and the SLD Cramér-Rao bound ($ ar{\epsilon}_{	ext{SLD}}$).
important_parameters: Depolarizing noise strength ($\lambda$) and the number of parallel uses ($k$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the class of parallel ancilla-assisted quantum strategies, and the attainment of the NH bound remains an open theoretical problem.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares the achieved risk ($ ar{\epsilon}^*$) against the two theoretical bounds ($ ar{\epsilon}_{	ext{SLD}}$ and $ ar{\epsilon}_{	ext{NH}}$) as a function of noise strength ($\lambda$) for $k=1$ to $4$, showing the convergence of curves.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the hierarchy of quantum estimation bounds, formulates the minimization problem via SDPs exploiting rotational symmetry, computes integrals exactly using quadrature methods, and compares the achieved risk against these theoretical limits across varying noise levels and uses.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous test case demonstrating how advanced information-theoretic bounds (like NH) can be numerically verified as achievable in quantum estimation protocols, which is crucial for designing optimal quantum sensors.
